text: In Gentzen's sequent calculus, the sequent Γ ⊢ Δ (with Γ, Δ finite sequences of formulas) intuitively means:
choices: assuming all formulas in Γ, at least one formula in Δ holds
assuming all formulas in Γ, all formulas in Δ hold
at least one formula in Γ implies all of Δ
Γ and Δ are logically equivalent
explanation: The standard reading of Γ ⊢ Δ is: if every formula in Γ holds (conjunction on the left), then at least one formula in Δ holds (disjunction on the right). The 'all of Δ' reading (option 2) and options 3 and 4 misstate this left-conjunction / right-disjunction semantics.
